newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Mirvac says profit rise possible.
newsitem.headline: Mirvac says profit rise possible.

text.p: Property manager and developer Mirvac Ltd said on Tuesday it expected to achieve a higher net profit in the 1996/97 financial year.
"I think we should be able to get an increase," managing director Robert Hamilton told a news conference.
"We are looking for a good year," said Hamilton who added, however, that he was reluctant to forecast the potential profit increase in percentage terms.
He said the company wanted to improve its margins from the housing division this year and had 1,167 dwellings under construction as part of major projects.
These dwellings had a sales value ot A$572 million.
Contracts had been exchanged on 767 of these dwellings, which allowed the company to be "very comfortable about 1996/97", finance director Dennis Broit said.
Mirvac, which has Lend Lease Corp Ltd as its largest shareholder with a 25 percent stake, earlier announced a 21 percent rise in 1995/96 net profit to A$21.7 million.

Broit said the company's market capitalisation had more than doubled in the last 12 months to nearly A$300 million as institutions had replaced some corporate and individual investors such as Brierley Investments Ltd and founder Henry Pollack. Lend Lease does not plan to increase its stake unless another party emerges with a stake of 15 percent or more.
Hamilton is the next largest shareholder with a stake of about 11 percent followed by First State, he said.
Hamilton said the company was "costing down to the last dollar" its plans for the Sydney 2000 Olympic Village.

Mirvac is the key partner in the Mirvac Village Industry Consortium which is seeking a contract from the New South Wales government to build the village at a cost estimated at up to A$550 million. Other members include CSR Ltd, James Hardie Industries Ltd, and Lend Lease.
This group is vying with a consortium led by Stockland Trust Group, Multiplex Construction and Daewoo Corp for the contract. The winning bidder will be announced at the end of 1996.
